div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Stage comes from opening question 4, what the demo must prove,
and question 5, the constraints. Chip: Prototype, MVP, Production
The developer can change it. Changing it later reopens only the
criteria whose applicability changed, and says how many
Running tasks continue unless a new decision affects their contract
One catalog, and the stage decides what applies,
the same idea as OWASP ASVS levels. The chip is the appetite
Options carry consequences, in the ADR sense

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Stage. Honesty stays.
The recommendation changes

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Scale, compliance, observability and multi-region
collapse to one line: not in this release
Simple local choices are recommended

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Basic privacy, errors, accessibility and deployment apply
Pragmatic defaults

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The full cross-cutting packs apply
Recommendations favor durability and auditability

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A risk trigger overrides the stage
Payments on a prototype still ask the payments questions

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Before a question is shown, code scores it
ask value = impact times uncertainty
impact = risk weight times dependents, plus one
uncertainty is 0 if evidence settles it, low if one option
dominates, high if the options really differ
Next questions are greedy maximum coverage, then this filter

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Must-ask, and not already
answered with evidence?

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Always ask, explicitly
Purpose and audience. Spending money. Real personal data
Identity and login provider. Hard to reverse. Legal or compliance
Or it contradicts what the developer already said
Autopilot never delegates one of these

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: How is this batch running?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Resolve with the recommendation
List it under Chosen for you. Never drop it silently

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Still shown, at the end of the batch, preselected
Accept all clears them

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Show it in the batch

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Soft cap per feature: about 10 on a Prototype,
about 25 in Production. Past the cap, remaining low-tier
questions go to Chosen for you. They are not dropped

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Every batch: recommended option preselected
An item already settled from evidence is shown, and needs nothing

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: CREDIT

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What the developer does

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Accepts every highlighted option in this batch
except must-ask, which stays for an explicit choice
Any of them can be changed first. Basis: explicit. Full credit

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Batch after batch until the architecture is complete
Stops only for must-ask, and says where it stopped
Opening five are must-ask, so Autopilot starts after them
Basis: delegated, with the risk bound and the stage
Full credit, and listed in Chosen for you

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: That answer is explicit. The rest of the batch stays

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Chosen for you stays visible. Any item reopens from the canvas
The plan preview flags tasks whose decisions were all delegated
A later explicit answer wins, and dependents are rechecked
'I never chose this' opens from the list, with batch and time
No matching recommend rule: the question is shown, not guessed
Two readings stay a conflict until the developer picks

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Versioned YAML, shared or project. On load: unique ids,
real criteria, acyclic prerequisites, real options,
must_ask only on high or critical. Never change an id's meaning
Lifecycle: draft, evaluated, active, deprecated
Active only after it changed a build on held-out projects
Promotion into the shared catalog is a reviewed edit, never automatic
Packs are the union of what opening review activates. Criteria deduped
Core, web, API, data and auth are deep. Payments are probe plus must-ask
Extension, mobile, desktop, CLI, AI and email are probe
Cross-cutting packs depend on the stage. About 200 in v1
A seam between two packs asks its questions once, not once per pack
Later: cloud, real-time, games, data pipelines

svg.text: How many questions, Accept all, and Autopilot
